verdicts.identification: Windows protected-image replacement race proof-of-concept source fragment
execution_trace: redirect_remediation requests an oplock on its caller-provided staged file and waits on its event.

It marks a caller-provided directory for POSIX deletion with NtSetInformationFile class 64, then sets a mount-point reparse record on the parent directory. The reparse destination bytes are supplied by the caller.
It opens the hardcoded PowerShell-directory bcrypt.dll under System32 in a KTM transaction, truncates the file, writes the caller-provided payload bytes to that handle, and commits.
A separate helper connects to Task Scheduler, retrieves Application Experience/MareBackup, and requests Run.
verdicts.limits: There is no main, caller, exploit harness, reparse destination, or payload in this fragment. No runtime success, actual privilege transition, or dependency of MareBackup on the overwritten DLL is established. The coordinated deletion/redirection race, protected-image payload overwrite, and task-run helper favor exploit intent; legitimate authorized research context is not supplied.
verdicts.trait_changes: Preserved two hostile protected-image write/task-run patterns. Moved generic oplock/delete/reparse co-occurrence to a notable filesystem capability, made ordinary oplock requests notable, required file-write evidence for the protected-image pattern, and removed the unproved DLL-load relation and T1574.001 mapping.

verdicts.identification: Windows Defender Cloud Files/object-namespace path-confusion exploit scaffold
execution_trace: hydrate prepares CF_OPERATION_TYPE_TRANSFER_DATA, copies connection/transfer keys and a data buffer, then calls CfExecute. Its callback signature is not a complete valid Cloud Files fetch-data callback.
The cleanup helper loads MpClient.dll and resolves manager, scan, and cleaning exports. Those pointers are discarded without invocation.
The helper attempts sync-root registration/connection and placeholder creation with zero-initialized registration and placeholder structures.
It resolves native directory and symbolic-link APIs and calls them with null output/attribute/target pointers.

The file carries deliberately combined globalroot/Restricted-object paths, a CLFS-to-UNC administrative-share alias, and an object-manager name with a stream suffix, but none is passed to the native alias calls.

SECURITY_WORLD_SID_AUTHORITY initializes an otherwise unused local. The EXPLICIT_ACCESS record gets GENERIC_ALL but no trustee SID; SetEntriesInAclW gets no output ACL pointer. DeviceIoControl uses INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE for the mount-point operation.
verdicts.limits: This is nonfunctional scaffolding, not a demonstrated working exploit. It contains no entry point, complete alias targets, usable ACL, scan invocation, final privileged victim, or deployment context. The unusual conjunction of Defender cleaning, hydration, restricted object aliases, CLFS, streams and mount redirection favors exploit-development intent over ordinary sync-provider code. Security-research authorization cannot be inferred from public-registry origin.
verdicts.trait_changes: Retained four hostile attempt-pattern findings and all neutral API/path observations. Renamed the ACL co-occurrence and its consuming Defender finding: neither now asserts an Everyone-writable root or a connected world trustee.

verdicts.identification: Encrypted ZIP carrying an x86-64 SHC-wrapped macOS AppleScript installer
execution_trace: main calls xsh; xsh calls chkenv for a code/data/PID-keyed re-execution cookie, initializes the SHC cipher state, and keys it with the embedded 256-byte password.
The custom RC4 state was reproduced from key/arc4 instructions. Decoding order follows xsh; both decrypted check strings compare equal, confirming plaintext recovery.

The decoded shell is /bin/bash with -c and a re-exec command. The expiry string is empty. The relaxed/redistributable flag is 1, so key_with_file is bypassed although the helper and stat import remain present.
The runtime decrypts a 3219-byte script, allocates its length plus 4096, fills the prefix with spaces, copies the script after that prefix, and passes the buffer through the execvp argument array.
The recovered script posts launch/status messages and the username to a remote HTTPS endpoint with certificate verification disabled.
It compiles an AppleScript app into an Apple-looking Application Support directory, sets LSUIElement, swaps its icon, and writes and loads an Apple-labeled RunAtLoad LaunchAgent.
The embedded AppleScript requests remote source, pipes it into osacompile -x, invokes the resulting script with osascript, removes it, and retries after errors.
The installer can remove a [CP] Build Pods Frameworks entry from an Xcode project when its AUTOCLEAN argument is true.
verdicts.limits: The later remote script is not present, so its ultimate behavior is unknown. This verdict rests on the recovered installer chain, covert login persistence, Apple identity disguise, hidden UI and conditional build-hook cleanup, rather than the generic SHC wrapper, unsigned status, archive encryption, domain reputation or scanner score.
verdicts.trait_changes: Replaced the generic hostile launcher with a suspicious SHC encrypted-execution rule in its behavior home. Moved optional file-keying support to notable crypto/KDF capability. Replaced the misleading third-party Roothelper/XCSSET label with the identical YARA predicate as SHC compiler metadata. Added a general SHC space-padding concealment rule; no domain, ciphertext, sample filename, or sample hash is used to convict.

coverage_and_classifier.floor: Race: two hostile findings. Defender scaffold: four hostile findings. ZIP and member: two suspicious findings covering encrypted execution and command-argument concealment. Neither generic wrapper property can honestly be hostile.
coverage_and_classifier.gap: The analyzer does not decode this SHC payload into a rule-visible source layer. Persistence, remote compilation/execution, masquerade, and project-hook cleanup are manually established but remain invisible on the original native bytes. Domain/ciphertext fingerprints would not be a generalizable fix.
coverage_and_classifier.classifier_after: Race is suspicious (level 1750), Defender scaffold hostile (level 1), and both the archive and standalone member benign (level -1). The archive member also gets a benign per-member score. All three analyst verdicts remain MALICIOUS.
coverage_and_classifier.losses: One generic race hostile moved to neutral mechanics; two generic SHC hostile labels became accurate compiler metadata plus suspicious concealment/execution; active environmental-keying suspicion became optional file-keying support. Every pre-edit behavioral observation has a retained or corrected home. The generic RC4/data/exec near miss no longer gets an encrypted-payload claim. The race control without file-write evidence no longer gets protected-image overwrite/task-chain claims.
coverage_and_classifier.emission_check: The first standalone baseline used a cached report with extra low-tier facts and two generic umbrella findings. An uncached HEAD snapshot reproduces the baseline without those extras. test-rules confirms binary-process-execution, fortify and small-macho-binary still match; engine filtering removes low-value OR wrappers and unreferenced baseline facts, while c-exec-variants and memcpy-chk preserve the actual capabilities.
coverage_and_classifier.model_warning: Installed atomscan engine 2.13.0 uses model bundle v18.18/spec v18 while its extractor expects v19. Scores and calibrated levels are reported, not treated as ground truth.

shared_rule_review.consumers: Exact consumers and directory ancestors were searched before relocation/narrowing. Only the protected-image consumer uses oplock-primitive. The ACL composite has one exact Defender consumer, updated with the renamed observation. The two old Mach-O composites have no exact consumers; binary-metric ancestor suppressors do not acquire behavior rules at their new locations. Compiler/native ancestor consumers are Windows/PE-specific and cannot suppress macOS SHC capabilities. The Ruby encoded-payload consumer cannot gain a Mach-O match.
shared_rule_review.outside_batch_positive: Built neurobin/shc 4.0.3 from its published source and packaged a harmless printf-only shell script. The original generic native rule and third-party signature both flagged it hostile; corrected rules retain accurate suspicious encryption and padding. A no-padding rebuild retains encrypted execution and loses only padding. These are generated controls, not reconstructed original specimens.
shared_rule_review.regressions: 12 static checks passed, including the three source/member artifacts, actual upstream-generated benign wrappers, unrelated RC4 and exec, ordinary oplock use, filesystem swap without protected-image context, missing image write, unused world authority, ordinary Cloud Files provider, and the recovered installer. No specimen or recovered payload was executed.
shared_rule_review.yara_preservation: The new SHC metadata matcher preserves every string, opcode and Boolean alternative from the disabled third-party predicate verbatim. Only the rule name/header/meta were changed; the local rule is scoped to Mach-O.
shared_rule_review.padding_atom: Final validation required the opcode sequence to be a named atomic trait. It is now a notable probable space-fill observation under micro-behaviors/mem/fill, with the same bounded instruction pattern plus a memset reference. The suspicious consumer still requires SHC metadata and exec. All 12 regression checks passed again; archive and standalone native scans were rerun.
shared_rule_review.validation_description_fix: Validation enforces 48-character/seven-word descriptions. New and renamed descriptions were shortened without changing matchers, scopes, IDs or severity; behavior details remain in comments and this review.

sources.purpose: Primary compiler source verifies standard runtime code, optional key_with_file, RC4 layout and hide_z argument padding; forager provenance retained in scratch.
Primary API documentation confirms the same DeviceIoControl oplock request is normal filesystem coordination.

reproduce: Compile shc.c from the recorded 4.0.3 URL with clang; run shc -r -f benign.sh; rebuild the generated benign.sh.x.c with clang -arch x86_64 -O0. For the second fixture, change only hide_z from 4096 to 0 before rebuilding. Generated output bytes vary with the compiler randomization.

Fresh scans: CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0 CLEAVE_SKIP_CACHE=1 SCAN_HOPPER= atomscan --no-update --mode slow -f json <path>. The scan validation override is only for the stale installed scanner budget; final validation uses the source-matched Cleave 3.0.0-beta.2 build.
